Events.RelatedDescription: Opened issue ".NET 11 Release Candidate 1" (#444) at dotnet/announcements
Events.RelatedBody:
> This issue is a locked mirror of https://github.com/dotnet/core/discussions/10569. See that thread for discussion.

We are pleased to announce the release of .NET 11 Release Candidate 1. Follow the main announcement and [blog announcement](https://aka.ms/dotnet/11/rc1).

This is our first of two release candidates which come with a [go-live support license](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/platform/support/policy/dotnet-core#previews) so you can confidently use this release for your production applications. This release of .NET 11 is supported in the new [Visual Studio 2026 Insiders](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/insiders/) release alongside Visual Studio Code with the C# Dev Kit. Check out the full release notes below and get started today.

This release contains the following highlights and improvements.

Browse the release notes for a full list of improvements in this release:

- [.NET MAUI](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/dotnetmaui.md)
- [ASP.NET Core](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/aspnetcore.md)
- [C#](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/csharp.md)
- [F#](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/fsharp.md)
- [Container images](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/containers.md)
- [EF Core & Data](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/efcore.md)
- [Libraries](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/libraries.md)
- [MSBuild](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/msbuild.md)
- [NuGet](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/nuget.md)
- [Runtime](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/runtime.md)
- [SDK](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/sdk.md)
- [Windows Forms](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/winforms.md)

## Get started

To get started with .NET 11, [install the .NET 11 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/11.0).

If you're on Windows using Visual Studio, we recommend installing the latest [Visual Studio 2026 Insiders](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/insiders/). You can also use Visual Studio Code and the [C# Dev Kit](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-dotnettools.csdevkit) extension with .NET 11.

# Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-69304 – ASP.NET Core Denial of Service Vulnerability ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in ASP.NET Core IIS out-of-process hosting and request decompression. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. The IIS Middleware for ASP.NET Core did not properly constrain decompression of certain types of request, leading to excess memory consumption and a Denial of Service. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/discussions/69155 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** Medium - **Score:** 5.9 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-409 (Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification)) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows / IIS out-of-process - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects any Microsoft .NET project if it uses any of affected package versions listed below ### .NET 11 RC1 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.30 | 8.0.31 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.30 | 8.0.31 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x64) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.30 | 8.0.31 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x86](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x86) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.30 | 8.0.31 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs. 2. If your application references the vulnerable package, update the package reference to the patched version. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command. Once you have installed the updated runtime or SDK, restart your apps for the update to take effect. Additionally, if you've deployed [self-contained applications](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/deploying/#self-contained-deployments-scd) targeting any of the impacted versions, these applications are also vulnerable and must be recompiled and redeployed. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. # Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-69806 – .NET Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in .NET SDK dotnet watch. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. The dotnet-watch AspireServerService exposes information through the use of certain arguments, that in turn can enable code injection. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/56167 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.0 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-200 (Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor); CWE-94 (Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Linux - **Architectures:** All ## Affected .NET SDKs The vulnerability affects Linux installations of the .NET SDK in the version ranges listed below. These are SDK versions, not NuGet package versions. ### .NET 11 RC1 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 11.0.1xx RC1 | Earlier .NET 11 previews | 11.0.100-rc.1 ### .NET 10 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 10.0.1xx | >= 10.0.100, <= 10.0.110 | 10.0.111 10.0.3xx | >= 10.0.300, <= 10.0.399 | 10.0.400 ### .NET 9 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 9.0.3xx | >= 9.0.300, <= 9.0.316 | 9.0.317 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using an SDK listed in [affected .NET SDKs](#affected-sdks) on Linux, you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. 2. Update each affected SDK feature band to the patched version listed above. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command. Once you have installed the updated SDK, restart dotnet watch and your applications for the update to take effect. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/sdk. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Microsoft disclaims all warranties, either express or implied, including the warranties of merchantability and fitness for a particular purpose. In no event shall Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers be liable for any damages whatsoever including direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, loss of business profits or special damages, even if Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers have been advised of the possibility of such damages. Some states do not allow the exclusion or limitation of liability for consequential or incidental damages so the foregoing limitation may not apply. ### External Links [CVE-2026-69806](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-69806) ### Acknowledgements Ky0toFu with Microsoft ### Revisions V1.0 (09/08/2026): Advisory published.

Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native can perform an out of bounds write while processing MSFZ PDB files. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/133438 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 8.8 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-122 (Heap-based Buffer Overflow) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects any Microsoft .NET project if it uses any of affected package versions listed below ### .NET 11 RC1 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native) | >= 17.10.0-beta1.24272.1, <= 18.9.0-beta1.26405.1 | 18.9.0-beta1.26405.2 ### .NET 10 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native) | >= 17.12.0-beta1.24603.5, <= 18.9.0-beta1.26405.1 | 18.9.0-beta1.26405.2 ### .NET 9 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native) | >= 17.12.0-beta1.24603.5, <= 18.9.0-beta1.26405.1 | 18.9.0-beta1.26405.2 ### .NET 8 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native) | >= 17.12.0-beta1.24603.5, <= 18.9.0-beta1.26405.1 | 18.9.0-beta1.26405.2 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET or Visual Studio. 2. If your application references Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native, update the package reference to version 18.9.0-beta1.26405.2 or later. Once you have installed the updated runtime, SDK, Visual Studio, or package, restart your apps for the update to take effect. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. # Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-58649 – .NET Information Disclosure Vulnerability ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in .NET SDK dotnet watch. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. The dotnet watch BrowserRefreshServer does not adequately validate cross-origin WebSocket origins, potentially allowing IL and PDB information disclosure. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/56166 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** Medium - **Score:** 6.5 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N` - **Weakness:** CWE-346 (Origin Validation Error) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows, Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected .NET SDKs The vulnerability affects installations of the .NET SDK in the version ranges listed below. These are SDK versions, not NuGet package versions. ### .NET 11 RC1 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 11.0.1xx RC1 | Earlier .NET 11 previews | 11.0.100-rc.1 ### .NET 10 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 10.0.1xx | >= 10.0.100, <= 10.0.110 | 10.0.111 10.0.3xx | >= 10.0.300, <= 10.0.399 | 10.0.400 ### .NET 9 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 9.0.1xx | >= 9.0.100, <= 9.0.119 | 9.0.120 9.0.3xx | >= 9.0.300, <= 9.0.316 | 9.0.317 ### .NET 8 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 8.0.1xx | >= 8.0.100, <= 8.0.129 | 8.0.130 8.0.4xx | >= 8.0.400, <= 8.0.423 | 8.0.424 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using an SDK listed in [affected .NET SDKs](#affected-sdks), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs. 2. Update each affected SDK feature band to the patched version listed above. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command. Once you have installed the updated SDK, restart dotnet watch and your applications for the update to take effect. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/sdk. Events.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "CodeGenerator.HasHome most likely lacking proper handling for `RefKindExtensions.StrictIn`" (#84486) at dotnet/roslyn
Events.RelatedBody:
I was experimenting with a fix for #84344 and ran into an incorrect behavior for `BoundDup` with `RefKind == RefKindExtensions.StrictIn`. I would expect the result of the function be true when ```IsAnyReadOnly(addressKind)```. Local rewriter creates `LocalSymbol`s with such `RefKind` and this is how we ended up with `BoundDup` with such `RefKind` during my experiment. Note, that it looks like the function has similar issue with `BoundLocal` nodes. However, a quick attempt to adjust the code for `BoundLocal` resulted to several test breaks in `ExtensionIndexersTests` and `ExtensionTests`.

I think my intuition about behavior of `CodeGenerator.HasHome` is correct, but it looks like we might have improper handling elsewhere.

We also should check other places where `RefKind.RefREadonly` is treated specially but `RefKindExtensions.StrictIn` isn't.

Alternatively, we can evaluate a possibility of getting rid of `RefKindExtensions.StrictIn` value and find a different way to represent the desired semantics without using a special internal `RefKind` value. Or, perhaps, we should never use it for a `LocalSymbol`.

Bottom line, more investigation is necessary here.

Issues.Title: [release/3.1] Reset current_no_gc_region_info after leaving no gc region implicitly
Issues.Body:
Backport https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/73602.

## Customer Impact
Customers reported occasional `System.InvalidOperationException` with message `The NoGCRegion mode was already in progress` when calling `GC.TryStartNoGCRegion`. This is preventing them from using this optimization and impacting their cold start latencies.

## Testing
Customers have tried the fix on .NET 6 overnight and reported the exception never appears again. Meanwhile, there is an unpatched machine and observed 72 exceptions of the same type in the same time interval, proving this does fix the bug.

## Risk
Low. This only impact customer using `TryStartNoGCRegion`, and this is the right thing to do.

Issues.Title: Migrate FabricBot Tasks to Config-as-Code
Issues.Body:
**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. If you have any questions or concerns with this pull request, please contact [MerlinBot Expert DRI](mailto:merlinbotdri@microsoft.com).

Issues.Title: Migrate FabricBot Tasks to Config-as-Code
Issues.Body:
**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/cli) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/cli) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. If you have any questions or concerns with this pull request, please contact [MerlinBot Expert DRI](mailto:merlinbotdri@microsoft.com).

Issues.Title: Confusing behavior when using AssemblyInfo.cs
Issues.Body:
I'm completely perplexed.

I created a .Net Standard 2.0 library project.

I explicity added an AssemblyInfo.cs file, we need this because we use this utility to "stamp" our assemblies when we build them:

https://github.com/ygoe/NetRevisionTool

That utility is run as a pre/post build event and temporarily replaces placeholders in the AssemblyInformationalVersion attribute with runtime values (like repo folder name, commit ID, branch etc etc).

The completed assembly then has this info "burned" into it as we go forward.

.Net Standard is not working with this.

2. The version of the generated nuget package is always set as 1.0.0.

This is just mind blowing, is there no way we can do this seemingly simple operation any more if adopt .Net Standard?

Issues.Title: Questions about tagging within this repository / future versions
Issues.Body:
I was looking through this repository to determine if .NET Standard 2.1 libraries support default interface methods - it looks like they do, given the presence of `System.Runtime.CompilerServices.RuntimeFeature.DefaultImplementationsOfInterfaces`, as well as my own experimenting in VS 2019. It seems I was mistaken when thinking that this was not the case, so I'm glad this repository is easily accessible to determine this.

But while doing this, I found it difficult to determine what commits were included in this particular .NET Standard version. I see that there's a tag `v2.1.0-prerelease.19126.1`, as well as branches `release/2.0.0`, `release/3.0`, and `release/3.0-preview9`. One of the machines I tested VS 2019 on had a `netstandard.dll` assembly, itself targeting .NETStandard v2.1.0, with AssemblyInformationalVersion `1.1.0+a5b5f2e1e369972c8ff1e2183979fab6099f52ef`; this commit is part of the `release/3.0` branch. However, another machine had a same-named assembly, targeting .NETCoreApp v3.0 and AssemblyInformationalVersion `3.0.0+4ac4c0367003fe3973a3648eb0715ddb0e3bbcea`, and I don't see that commit hash in this repository.

Additionally, [this blog post](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/the-future-of-net-standard/) states that 2.1 will be the last version, but there is another prerelease tag `v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1` and [on GitHub](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/releases/tag/v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1) it's labelled .NET 5.0 Preview 2.

So I have a few questions for understanding this repository:

1. Since .NET Standard 2.1 is released, are there plans to continue development in this repository for e.g. the shared BCL going forward with .NET 5+?
2. Are there multiple kinds of `netstandard.dll` for a single .NET Standard version? E.g. are there separate versions for .NET Framework to reference and for .NET Core / .NET 5+ to reference?
3. Do the tags / branch names in this repository correspond to a .NET Standard version or something else?
4. It looks like there are patch releases; are there patch versions of a single .NET Standard version?
5. Are there other repositories which are being used to create `netstandard.dll`?
6. Is there a way to determine, from the repository, which commit is the one used for a given release?

Thank you for your consideration.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Questions about tagging within this repository / future versions" (#1777)

Issues.Title: Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1
Issues.Body:
# Summary

.NET Standard version is not resolved correctly when a transitive dependency targets multiple .NET Standard versions.

# Environment

- Windows 10 (19042.746)
- .NET 5 SDK 5.0.201

# Minimal reproducible example
[bug.zip](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/files/6209239/bug.zip)

This is a three-project solution:
- `TestProject1` targeting `netcoreapp3.1`
- `ClassProject1` targeting `netstandard2.0`
- `ClassProject2` targeting *both* `netstandard2.0` and `netstandard2.1`

The project dependency chain is: `TestProject1 -> ClassProject1 -> ClassProject2`

A method (`ClassProject2Test1`) on `ClassProject2` is hidden behind a `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.

# The issue

The unit test failed with a `MissingMethodException`

```
[xUnit.net 00:00:00.38]     TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [FAIL]
  Failed TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [2 ms]
  Error Message:
   System.MissingMethodException : Method not found: 'Void ClassLibrary2.Class2.Class2Test1()'.
  Stack Trace:
     at ClassLibrary1.Class1.Class1Test1()
   at TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1() in C:\Users\rex\source\netstandard-bug-repro\TestProject1\UnitTest1.cs:line 12
```

# Expected result

The compiler should have resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.0)*` 

# Actual result

The compiler resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.1)*` 

Which causes the exception because the offending method, `ClassProject2Test1`, was hidden by the `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1" (#1787)

https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/en-US/vulnerability/CVE-2019-0820
https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/111
https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2019-0820
https://snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-DOTNET-SYSTEMTEXTREGULAREXPRESSIONS-174708
https://www.whitesourcesoftware.com/vulnerability-database/CVE-2019-0820

The dotnet commit that fixed the vulnerability is https://github.com/dotnet/corefx/commit/19d4b1163d8a03dd90ff5fd1785eea6305112545

### Issue:
We use whitesource and it has caught this issue with high severity. We don't consume System.Text.RegularExpressions directly but packages that use this. Therefore as a transitive dependency due to NetStandard library, which is being used by several other dotnet packages like Castle Windsor, MassTransit etc., Once an update is available the others could followup and update.

### Code:

[The latest version 2.0.3 of Net standard ](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) still seem to be using System.Text.RegularExpressions version 4.3.0 as per https://github.com/dotnet/standard/blob/master/src/apicompat/netstandard/netstandard.depproj

### Fix
Please update[ library](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) targeting .netStandard 1.6 to update System.Text.RegularExpression package to latest secured version 4.3.1 to fix the security issue or kindly suggest alternatives.

Issues.Title: linq using GetValueOrDefault  in Where clause problem
Issues.Body:
Hello,

I am currently using .NET core 2.2.x and EF Core. 2.2.6. I have a function that returns a List<Animal> from the database with no issue. It returns 11 results. However, when I try to use `.Where(p => p.DeletedAt.GetValueOrDefault(DateTime.Now) => DateTime.Now).ToList()`, it still should return 11 results, however it returns 0. I also eliminated the possibility that there is something wrong with my where clause (logic) because it works perfectly on 4.6.1 EF Core 2.2.6. Furthermore, I confirmed that it is only where I am comparing a nullable type using that function and I am guessing that I missed a thread someone opened on this issue. I am aware .NET core 2.2 is not LTS. I also thought this goes here because it's not AFAIK, an EF core issue but rather an Ienumerable/Linq issue.

Update: As it turns out your notion of `DateTime.Now` getting evaluated twice is true. To rectify that, I will now be using `DateTime.Now.Date`. This is odd because this exact code works on 4.6.1. You're probably right. SMH. Thank you @GrabYourPitchforks! You may now close.

Issues.Title: System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings slow
Issues.Body:
_This issue has been moved from [a ticket on Developer Community](https://developercommunity2.visualstudio.com/t/SystemDrawingPrintingPrinterSettings-/890524)._ --- Hello I'm debugging a problem with the printer settings. Some calls are significant slower if the default printer is a network printer, even if I explicit set a local printer name. After studying referencesource I think I found the culprit. I call: var printerSettings = new System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings(); printerSettings.PrinterName = "LOCALPRINTER"; // the next call is slow if the OS default printer is a network printer var res = printerSettings.DefaultPageSettings.PrinterResolution Internally FastDeviceCapabilities is called. FastDeviceCapabilities calls GetOutputPort. But GetOutput port return the port of the default printer and not the port of the given printer! In addition, DeviceCapabilities is then called with a wrong combination of printer name and port, don't know if this could lead to additional problems. Resolution: GetOutputPort should return the port of the given printer and not accessing the default printer at all. Best Regards, Raphael --- ### Original Comments #### Raphael Affolter on 1/20/2020, 04:03 AM:

I forgot to mention: .Net Framework 4.6.1

#### Feedback Bot on 1/20/2020, 06:51 PM:

Because we print a lot, we really suffer from this performance penalty.

Also reading PaperSizes and PaperSources from the printer settings is slow caused by the same problem.

Best Regards,

Raphael

Issues.Title: Build issues when referencing project that targets multiple frameworks C# WPF
Issues.Body:
I'm working on converting a large WPF solution's projects to SDK style and ran into some issues.

The solution is large with multiple projects(old style) all targeting .net452 and some nugets(some made by me) installed, targeting both .net452 and .netstandard2.1 This all seems to work fine, somehow the nuget manages to install the correct version targeting .net452.

I have decided to slowly convert the projects inside the solution to SDK style targeting .net452 and .netstandard2.1 just like the nugets.

This is where the problem starts, one project was converted so far that is referenced by multiple other projects. Localy everything seems to build and run fine, however when Azure DevOps(VS version 2019) is used to build the solution there are 2 scenarios:

1. The famous error message is shown:

                "Error CS0012: The type 'Object' is defined in an assembly that is not referenced. You must add a reference to assembly 
                 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0"

2. It builds fine but on app launch it crashes with:

                 "Could not load file or assembly 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=cc7b13ffcd2ddd51' 
                 or one of its dependencies. The system cannot find the file specified."

I'm suspecting that the problem is related to referencing the SDK project, it looks like that somehow it references the .netstandard2.1 instead of the .net452.

The reason this is my suspicion is that if targetframework is set to only .net452 on the referenced project everything works fine. Google has led me to two possible solutions to tell the project what framework to use from the reference:

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj"
                  AdditionalProperties="TargetFramework=net452">
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
and

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj">
      <SetTargetFramework>TargetFramework=net452</SetTargetFramework>
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <<Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
This doesn't look like it's doing anything and the problem still persists. At the moment I ran out of ideas and I'm here asking for help. Please let me know what I'm doing wrong or what else I can try.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Build issues when referencing project that targets multiple frameworks C# WPF" (#1776)

**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/corefx) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/corefx) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. Issues.Title: Fix RSA OAEP decryption in OpenSSL with non-power-of-two keys lengths
Issues.Body:
## Customer Impact

A customer reported in dotnet/runtime#71607 that decrypting RSA OAEP with SHA2 and a 3072-bit key on Linux resulted in a OAEP de-padding error, while other platforms were able to perform these operations successfully.

Investigation in to the issue led to uncover that RSA OAEP decryption that uses the managed implementation does not work with non-power-of-two keys because we do not slice a rented buffer accordingly. The current implementation only works because `CryptoPool.Rent` happens to give back power-of-two arrays which are exactly the same size as the key.

The fix is to slice the data to the correct size.

This does not affect dotnet/runtime because the managed implementation of RSA OAEP is no longer used for OpenSSL RSA decryption. This change was introduced in dotnet/runtime#50063.

## Testing

Unit tests were introduced to test RSA OAEP encryption with a 3072-bit RSA key. These tests will be forward-ported to dotnet/runtime.

## Risk

Minimal. The change is localized and understood that a `Slice` was missing.

Issues.Title: Fix RpcServer response-write race that can crash BuildHost on shutdown
Issues.Body:
`VisualStudioMSBuildWorkspaceTests.Test_VisualBasic_ConditionalAttributeNotEmitted` (and similar tests) intermittently fail with `Exception while shutting down the BuildHost process`, which the test harness escalates to a hard failure via `WorkspaceFailed`.

## Root cause
- `RpcServer` (BuildHost's side of the custom RPC channel) wrote responses through a `TextWriter` wrapping the raw `PipeStream`, then called `Flush()`.
- `PipeStream.Flush()` throws `IOException: Pipe is broken` if the client already disconnected — expected during shutdown (e.g. client gave up waiting for the shutdown response), not an actual error.
- This is the same bug class fixed on the client side (`RpcClient`) in #77040/#77151, but the server's response-write path was never updated to match, so the exception surfaces during `BuildHostProcess.DisposeAsync()`, gets logged via `LogError`, and the test harness re-throws on the resulting `WorkspaceFailed` diagnostic.

## Fix
- `RpcServer` now writes response bytes directly to the underlying `PipeStream` instead of going through a `TextWriter`, mirroring `RpcClient`'s existing write path.
- Wraps the write in a `catch (IOException)` that swallows the exception when the pipe is already broken, since there's nobody left to receive the response.

```csharp
try
{
    using (await _streamWritingSemaphore.DisposableWaitAsync().ConfigureAwait(false))
    {
        await _stream.WriteAsync(responseJsonBytes, 0, responseJsonBytes.Length).ConfigureAwait(false);
    }
}
catch (IOException)
{
    // The pipe was already broken; nobody is left to receive the response.
}
```

## Tests
- Added `ResponseWriteAfterClientDisconnectsDoesNotThrow` in `RpcTests.cs`, exercising a server response write after the client has disconnected — mirroring the existing `RequestThatClosesServerDoesNotThrow` client-side regression test.

Issues.Title: TextChange.NewText has an unexpected nullable annotation
Issues.Body:
This member:

https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/97b4837e6812fbf3b8fd567e03b8c1e1d1089c65/src/Compilers/Core/Portable/Text/TextChange.cs#L31

is marked as nullable, but there's no clear indication what we intend by that. The constructor throws if you try to pass null, so it seems like it's only allowing null to handle the case of a default-constructed TextChange. SourceText.WithChanges has some code to handle that being null and treat that as an empty string. (But if the only way you can get this is a default-constructed struct, then what's the point since you're replacing nothing with nothing?)

But some other code has odd asserts that we expect non-null values:

https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/0c1dd5b7d74b0b0614845603fb13082b0acb9a8c/src/Compilers/Core/Portable/Text/TextChange.cs#L89-L93

But not if you call this other method that should do the same thing!

https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/0c1dd5b7d74b0b0614845603fb13082b0acb9a8c/src/Compilers/Core/Portable/Text/TextChangeRangeExtensions.cs#L103-L106

If the intent of the nullable annotation was to ensure we're "safe" in regards to default constructed structs, it seems like in practice this didn't result in good safety.

Issues.Title: Where should F# persist per-document data across sessions?
Issues.Body:
## Summary

F# has no way to persist per-document data across VS sessions, so Navigate To's solution-load-phase search (#85213) has nothing to answer from and always cold-parses.

## Background and Motivation

F# already ships a file-backed, checksum-keyed cache of its own for this (one file per document, not SQLite) — built because nothing in Roslyn was available to plug into. `IChecksummedPersistentStorage` solves the same problem for `TopLevelSyntaxTreeIndex`.

## Proposed Feature

An external-access seam over `IChecksummedPersistentStorage`'s per-document read/write/checksum-match, scoped to F#'s own key name — no C#/VB data exposed, same shape as #85213's search-only seam.

## Alternative Designs

If Roslyn won't expose this, F# builds its own SQLite-backed storage modeled on Roslyn's — not the current simple file cache. Either way, this doesn't block on Roslyn.

Issues.Title: Show another language's source for a metadata symbol in Peek Definition, Code Definition Window and Find All References
Issues.Body:
## Summary

In a solution that mixes C# and F#, Go To Definition from C# on a symbol an F# project defines opens the F# source. Peek Definition, the Code Definition Window and the definition row in Find All References show decompiled C# for the same symbol. I'd like to fix this through the existing hook for other languages, `ISymbolNavigationService.GetExternalNavigationSymbolLocationAsync`, instead of adding a special case to each feature.

## Background and Motivation

F# projects have no Roslyn compilation, so a C# project sees an F# symbol only as metadata. Go To Definition covers this case. Before it falls back to metadata-as-source, `VisualStudioSymbolNavigationService.GetNavigableLocationAsync` asks every `ICrossLanguageSymbolNavigationService`. The only one is the F# ExternalAccess adapter.

Three other features show a definition, and none of them goes through that method. Each asks `GetExternalNavigationSymbolLocationAsync(DefinitionItem)` for a file and position instead:

- Peek Definition: `PeekableItemFactory`
- Code Definition Window: `DefinitionContextTracker`
- Find All References: `VisualStudioDefinitionsAndReferencesFactory`, through `IExternalDefinitionItemProvider`. Go To Definition uses the same provider for its third-party item.

`GetExternalNavigationSymbolLocationAsync` only knows the RQName / `IVsSymbolicNavigationNotify` route. That route needs a source location, so it never answers for a metadata symbol, and the three features fall back to metadata-as-source. They couldn't ask `ICrossLanguageSymbolNavigationService` either. That service returns an `INavigableLocation`, which can navigate somewhere but can't say where.

Repro:
1. An F# library project with `type Counter() = member _.Increment() = ()` and a C# project that references it.
2. In C#, put the caret on `Counter` and press Alt+F12 (Peek Definition): it shows `Counter [decompiled]`.
3. Press F12 on the same symbol: it opens the F# file.

## Proposed Feature

1. Add a second member to `ICrossLanguageSymbolNavigationService` that says where the definition is. It returns a `DocumentSpan`, since F# files are documents of the solution:

   ```csharp
   Task<DocumentSpan?> TryGetDefinitionSpanAsync(
       string assemblyName, string documentationCommentId, CancellationToken cancellationToken);
   ```

2. `VisualStudioSymbolNavigationService.GetExternalNavigationSymbolLocationAsync` asks the cross-language services last, after its two RQName lookups, and only for a `DefinitionItem` created for a metadata symbol. It gets that symbol from the item's `MetadataSymbolKey` properties. The code that resolves them moves from `DefaultDefinitionItem` to `DefinitionItem` so both can use it. The span is converted to the `(filePath, LinePosition)` the method already returns. The callers don't change.

3. In the F# ExternalAccess layer, add `IFSharpCrossLanguageSymbolNavigationService2 : IFSharpCrossLanguageSymbolNavigationService` with the same member, returning `FSharpDocumentSpan?`. The adapter casts to it and returns `null` when the F# service doesn't implement it. It is a separate interface because FSharp.Editor ships separately from Roslyn. A member added to the existing interface would fail type load for an FSharp.Editor built against the previous version, which is the same reason `IFSharpAdvancedNavigateToSearchService` was added separately in #85213.

The F# side is written and tested against a local build (dotnet/fsharp#20520).

Two effects I'd like the team's view on:

- **Go To Definition.** Go To Definition also asks `IExternalDefinitionItemProvider`, and the presenter prefers an external item. So C# → F# F12 would open the file through `ExternalDefinitionItem` instead of the F# `INavigableLocation`. It lands on the same file and position, but `ExternalDefinitionItem` opens a regular tab rather than honoring `PreferProvisionalTab`. If that isn't acceptable, the cross-language lookup could be limited to the callers that only show a location.
- **Find All References.** On an F# symbol, the list gets an external definition row pointing at the F# file. To do that, it resolves the `SymbolKey` of each metadata definition and asks F#, which checks the assembly name before doing any work.

## Alternative Designs

- **Ask the cross-language services in `PeekableItemFactory` only.** This is what #85257 did first. It duplicates `GetExternalNavigationSymbolLocationAsync` and leaves the Code Definition Window and Find All References out.
- **Return `(string filePath, LinePosition)` from the new member**, to match `GetExternalNavigationSymbolLocationAsync`. This loses the document. `DocumentSpan` is what Roslyn already uses for definitions (`DefinitionItem.SourceSpans`).
- **Replace `TryGetNavigableLocationAsync` with the span member** and build Go To Definition's `INavigableLocation` through `IDocumentNavigationService`. That would leave one member instead of two. It isn't proposed here because F# uses its own navigation for declarations that aren't documents of the solution, such as an F# assembly referenced as a DLL.

Issues.Title: Build Peek Definition on Go To Definition so both show the same target
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Make Peek Definition show whatever Go To Definition would go to, so the two never disagree.

## Background and Motivation

Peek and Go To Definition work out the target separately:

- **Go To Definition:** `GoToDefinitionFeatureHelpers.GetDefinitionsAsync` → `DefinitionItem`s → `ISymbolNavigationService.GetNavigableLocationAsync` for a metadata symbol.
- **Peek:** `PeekableItemFactory`, with its own source / external / metadata-as-source branches.

So they drift apart. For example, F12 on an F# symbol from C# opens the F# source, because `GetNavigableLocationAsync` asks `ICrossLanguageSymbolNavigationService`. Peek on the same symbol shows decompiled C#.

Peek can't simply call Go To Definition today, because Go To Definition ends in an `INavigableLocation`: it can navigate to the target but can't say where it is.

## Proposed Feature

1. Split "find the target" from "navigate to it" in `ISymbolNavigationService`:
   ```csharp
   Task<FileLinePositionSpan?> GetDefinitionLocationAsync(ISymbol symbol, Project project, CancellationToken cancellationToken);
   ```
   It returns the source location, the other language's location, or the location in the metadata-as-source file. `GetNavigableLocationAsync` navigates to whatever it returns. The Object Browser option stays navigation-only.
2. Add a location-returning member to `ICrossLanguageSymbolNavigationService`: `Task<DocumentSpan?> TryGetDefinitionSpanAsync(assemblyName, documentationCommentId, ct)`. F# gets it through a separate `IFSharpCrossLanguageSymbolNavigationService2`, so an older FSharp.Editor still loads.
3. Peek takes its definitions from `GoToDefinitionFeatureHelpers.GetDefinitionsAsync` and shows each one's location inline. Its own resolution in `PeekableItemFactory` goes away.

## Alternative Designs

- Ask F# from Peek only (the first version of #85257). That fixes this case but keeps two pipelines.
- Ask F# from `GetExternalNavigationSymbolLocationAsync` (the current #85257). That fixes Peek, the Code Definition Window and Find All References, but Peek still resolves its target on its own.

Issues.Title: Test that a diagnostic without a help link has no code description
Issues.Body:
#83593 changed the argument `CreateLspDiagnostic` passes to `HelpLinkToCodeDescription`, and every diagnostic without a help link then reached Visual Studio with an empty `codeDescription.href`, which its client cannot deserialize. #85734 fixed the conversion and covers `HelpLinkToCodeDescription` directly, but a change at the call site would not fail those tests.

`TestDocumentDiagnosticsWithoutHelpLinkHaveNoCodeDescription` pulls a diagnostic from an analyzer whose descriptor has no help link through the document pull diagnostics handler, for both VS and non-VS clients, and asserts the reported diagnostic carries no `CodeDescription`. It fails on `main` with the `IsNullOrEmpty` check reverted to `!= null`. The existing `TestDocumentDiagnosticsForOpenFilesWithFSAOff` already covers the other side, a compiler diagnostic that does have a link.

Test only; nothing else changes. Follows #85666, which is closed in favor of #85734.

Issues.Title: Read Razor asset-path metadata from the code document
Issues.Body:
Raw HTML asset paths opted into compile-time expansion through `[AcceptsAssetPath]` remain literal when components compile through `RazorSourceGenerator`. Discovery correctly produces the carrier descriptors and `ProcessTagHelpers` attaches the complete project-wide collection to each `RazorCodeDocument`, but `ComponentTildePathPass` looks for an engine feature that the generation engine does not register.

Read the full collection directly from `RazorCodeDocument.GetRequiredTagHelpers()`. Documents without that optional project-wide input leave tilde paths unchanged. Direct project-engine tests that exercise this path explicitly attach feature-discovered tag helpers through a test-only phase rather than changing production discovery. The pass rebuilds the small asset-path allowlist from the document input on each execution.

Coverage exercises clean source-declared and referenced convention metadata. The complete Razor compiler suite passes 3,984 tests; the complete source-generator suite passes 228 tests with one existing skip; all 18 existing tilde compiler tests pass; and the analyzer-enabled affected build completes with no warnings or errors.

Issues.Title: IDE0380 False Positive in New C# 16 Memory Model
Issues.Body:
**Version Used**: VS Insiders [12210.170] / .NET SDK 11.0.100-rc.1.26425.128

**Steps to Reproduce**:

Program.cs
```csharp
using System;
using System.Runtime.InteropServices;

ReadOnlySpan<int> numbers = [1, 2, 3];
fixed (int* n = numbers)
{
    byte* b = (byte*)n;
    unsafe
    {
        Console.WriteLine(ReadInt(b));     // 1
        Console.WriteLine(ReadInt(b + 4)); // 2
        Console.WriteLine(ReadInt(b + 8)); // 3
        Console.WriteLine(ReadInt((byte*)0));
    }
}

static unsafe int ReadInt(byte* b)
{
    unsafe
    {
        ReadOnlySpan<byte> s = new(b, sizeof(int));
        return MemoryMarshal.Read<int>(s);
    }
}
```
.csproj
```xml
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">

  <PropertyGroup>
    <AllowUnsafeBlocks>true</AllowUnsafeBlocks>
    <EnforceCodeStyleInBuild>true</EnforceCodeStyleInBuild>
    <Features>$(Features);updated-memory-safety-rules</Features>
    <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
    <LangVersion>preview</LangVersion>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
    <OutputType>Exe</OutputType>
    <TargetFramework>net11.0</TargetFramework>
    <TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
    <WarningsAsErrors />
  </PropertyGroup>

</Project>
```

.editorconfig
```ini
[*.cs]
dotnet_analyzer_diagnostic.category-Style.severity = warning
dotnet_diagnostic.IDE0380.severity = error
```

**Diagnostic Id**: IDE0380: 'unsafe' modifier is unnecessary (https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/fundamentals/code-analysis/style-rules/ide0380)

**Expected Behavior**: No warning with the new memory model as compilation is no longer the sole indicator for whether the `unsafe` keyword is appropriate

**Actual Behavior**: Warning

See Discussion here: https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/discussions/85731
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "IDE0380 False Positive in New C# 16 Memory Model" (#85732)

Issues.Title: Fix ref safety analysis of mutable non-assignable receivers
Issues.Body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/issues/85694.

Previously, `ReceiverIsSubjectToCloning` classified `using` and `foreach` variables as cloned, because they are not assignable. However, a non-readonly struct method on such receiver is performed directly, no copy is created. This PR fixes the `ReceiverIsSubjectToCloning` helper to correctly classify those variables as not cloned.

Due to the incorrect temporary copy, ref safety analysis produced an escape error.

Issues.Title: Add the documentation directive to the Razor compiler
Issues.Body:
Adds `@documentation` in Razor 12 so components and views can document their generated class without losing source mappings. The XML stays file-local and C# validates it. The first local directive wins, imports cannot suppress it, and bodies containing an unsafe `*/` aren't emitted. Includes the RZ1047/RZ1048/RZ1049 diagnostics and recovery, declaration-splitting and mapping coverage.

Depends on #85721 (`davidwengier/razor-xml-parsing`). Part of #85414; editor classification, folding, completion, formatting and quick fixes follow separately.

**Validation:** 4,514 compiler tests, 25 VS Code document-diagnostic tests and 47 Visual Studio document-diagnostic tests passed, with analysers enabled and baseline generation off. Both compiler target frameworks and all three affected test projects build. The preparatory slice passed 587 existing syntax/directive checks, and both basic examples passed before adding the rest of the matrix.

Issues.Title: Add XML parsing mode to the Razor markup parser
Issues.Body:
Adds an isolated XML-only mode to the existing markup parser. It keeps Razor transitions literal, matches XML tag names case-sensitively and tracks whether the body is complete enough for recovery, without changing ordinary HTML parsing.

Also includes two separately committed fixes: preserve C# tokenizer line state after all C# newlines, and avoid consuming overlapping CDATA or processing-instruction terminators.

Built on #85720 (`davidwengier/razor-language-version-12`). This is groundwork for #85414, not the documentation directive itself: it doesn't register or recognise `@documentation`, or add directive syntax, diagnostics, lowering or editor features.

**Validation:**
- After the independent fixes: 16 tokenizer tests and 49 HTML tests passed.
- Product-only compiler build passed for `net10.0` and `netstandard2.0`, with zero warnings or errors.
- Final layer: 102 focused tests and all 4,009 Razor compiler tests passed on `net10.0`, with no failures or skips.

All builds and tests ran with `RunAnalyzersDuringBuild=true`; test runs used `--no-restore` and `GenerateBaselines=false`. Touched files were formatted, BOMs and line endings were preserved, and all six files match the frozen implementation exactly.

Issues.Title: Externalize localized resources from the NativeAOT CLI
Issues.Body:
## Summary

This change reduces the size of `dotnet-aot` by loading localized CLI strings from the managed satellite assemblies already present in the SDK layout instead of embedding duplicate satellite payloads into the NativeAOT image.

It adds:

- a shared string-resource runtime in `Microsoft.DotNet.Cli.CoreUtils`;
- an analyzer-only RESX generator for cached CLI resource accessors;
- PE-backed neutral and satellite resource readers that do not load or execute the managed assemblies;
- three private NativeAOT resource modes:
  - `Embedded`
  - `ExternalLocalized` — the new default
  - `ExternalAll` — measurement-only
- strict neutral-resource preflight before the NativeAOT commit point;
- tolerant exact → parent → neutral fallback for localized satellites; and
- mode-aware NativeAOT tests, layouts, and performance tooling.

The resource reader and generator were adapted from the prototype in `JeremyKuhne/touki`. Only the required string-resource closure was brought into the SDK, using SDK namespaces and license headers. This adds no runtime package dependency or new runtime assembly.

## Change size

The upstream diff contains 108 files, 12,151 added lines, and 69 deleted lines:

| Area | Files | Added | Deleted | Share of added lines |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Product code and project wiring | 75 | 9,165 | 51 | 75.4% |
| Tests and test selection | 26 | 2,499 | 11 | 20.6% |
| Reusable validation/performance tooling | 1 | 384 | 0 | 3.2% |
| Documentation and contributor guidance | 6 | 103 | 7 | 0.8% |

The product portion breaks down as:

| Product area | Added | Deleted |
|---|---:|---:|
| CoreUtils resource runtime | 5,961 | 0 |
| Analyzer-only resource generator | 2,541 | 0 |
| NativeAOT provider and resource modes | 562 | 38 |
| Managed-owner and project wiring | 101 | 13 |

The adapted low-level runtime and generator account for 8,502 lines, or 92.8% of the product additions. The NativeAOT behavior change itself is approximately 600 lines, with another approximately 100 lines of managed/project integration.

## Motivation

The final SDK already contains the managed CLI owner assemblies and their localized satellite assemblies. NativeAOT was also receiving satellite inputs through `@(IlcSatelliteAssembly)`, causing the same localized payloads to be embedded into `dotnet-aot.dll`.

Reusing the existing SDK-layout files removes that duplication while preserving the managed CLI's resource names, generated properties, culture fallback, and localized output.

## Design

### Shared resource runtime

The runtime implementation lives in `Microsoft.DotNet.Cli.CoreUtils` under:

```text
Microsoft.DotNet.Cli.Resources
Microsoft.DotNet.Cli.Resources.Internal
```

It supports:

- indexed string lookup from embedded `.resources`;
- neutral resources read from managed owner assemblies as PE data;
- localized resources read from managed satellite assemblies as PE data;
- assembly name, culture, version, and public-key-token validation;
- exact, parent, and neutral fallback;
- concurrency-safe table and culture caching; and
- strict or fallback-on-localized-failure probing.

External assemblies are parsed as trusted deployment data. They are never loaded or executed, and serialized user values are never activated.

The resource runtime is compiled only for `$(SdkTargetFramework)`, leaving the net472 CoreUtils build unchanged.

### Generated accessors

`Microsoft.DotNet.Cli.Resources.Generator` is a new analyzer-only `netstandard2.0` project.

It emits strongly typed accessors with:

- one cached field per resource property;
- constant-time cache replacement on culture changes;
- a process-wide manager provider selected before first access; and
- no runtime dependency on the generator assembly.

The managed CLI uses normal runtime-satellite behavior when no provider is registered.

### NativeAOT provider lifecycle

`NativeEntryPoint` now:

1. applies the UI-language override;
2. resolves the versioned SDK directory;
3. configures or preflights the selected resource mode;
4. falls back to the managed CLI immediately if `ExternalAll` preflight fails;
5. only then initializes telemetry, first-run behavior, and parsing.

This keeps neutral-resource failure before the NativeAOT commit point and avoids replaying an invocation after output or mutation.

### Resource modes

| Mode | Neutral strings | Localized strings | Intended use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Embedded` | Native image | Existing embedded inputs plus managed satellites for referenced SDK owners | Baseline |
| `ExternalLocalized` | Native image | Existing managed SDK satellites | Default |
| `ExternalAll` | Existing managed owner assemblies | Existing managed SDK satellites | Measurement only |

In both external modes, NativeAOT satellite inputs are removed before the ILC response file is written.

`ExternalAll` additionally passes a content-hashed substitution file that removes the catalogued SDK-owned neutral resource tables. Hashing the copied substitution filename ensures edits invalidate incremental native compilation.

The final SDK continues to contain one managed copy of each owner/satellite family and no `dotnet-aot.resources.dll`.

## User-visible behavior

NativeAOT command help now honors `DOTNET_CLI_UI_LANGUAGE` and uses the same managed satellite strings as the managed CLI.

The retained matrix compared exit code, stdout, and stderr for:

- invariant plus all 13 shipped cultures;
- `--version`;
- root help; and
- `sln --help`.

All 126 comparisons matched the managed CLI exactly.

## Size results

Windows x64 Release NativeAOT publishes:

| Mode | Native size | Delta from Embedded | Mstat resources |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `Embedded` | 20,107,264 B | — | 97 / 3,551,857 B |
| `ExternalLocalized` | 17,324,544 B | **-2,782,720 B (-13.84%)** | 32 / 789,881 B |
| `ExternalAll` | 17,065,472 B | **-3,041,792 B (-15.13%)** | 22 / 524,359 B |

The adapted-source implementation is also 2–2.5 KB smaller than the earlier binary-backed prototype.

No `touki.dll` remains in the managed dependency graph or SDK layout. The resource runtime is part of the existing CoreUtils assembly.

## Startup results

The retained Windows x64 matrix used:

- 30 launches per mode/culture/scenario;
- balanced launch ordering;
- warm fresh-process and practical-cold states;
- invariant, French, Japanese, and Traditional Chinese cultures; and
- 2,160 measured launches after warmup.

A bounded focused rerun was retained for noisy Japanese `sln --help` cases.

| Candidate | Cases passing both 5% and 1.0 ms gates | Decision |
|---|---:|---|
| `ExternalLocalized` | **24/24** | Default |
| `ExternalAll` | 8/24 | Measurement only |

A follow-up `OptimizationPreference=Speed` experiment made every measured `sln --help` case 4.02–5.74 ms slower and grew the native images by 22–26%, so the product remains optimized for size.

## Validation

- CoreUtils resource tests: **18/18 passed**
- Resource generator tests: **56/56 passed**
- CoreUtils net472 build: **0 warnings/errors**
- Managed `dotnet-aot.Tests`: **181 passed, 15 expected skips, 0 failed**
- Native resource tests:
  - `Embedded`: **15 passed, 1 mode-specific skip**
  - `ExternalLocalized`: **16/16 passed**
  - `ExternalAll`: **16/16 passed**
- Clean managed CLI, AOT product, and AOT test builds: **0 warnings/errors**
- Clean NativeAOT publish in all three modes
- Full default Release redist build
- Real muxer AOT and managed-fallback smoke
- Flat, separated, and self-locating SDK layouts
- 126/126 functional culture/command comparisons
- Nine no-managed-fallback preflights
- PowerShell/XML parsing, Markdown links, and `git diff --check`

The full native test application retains three unrelated local managed-fallback failures because this machine reports `Access is denied` when the native `dn` test host loads `hostfxr`. The new resource scenarios pass, and managed fallback works through the real redist muxer.

Performance and native execution evidence in this change is Windows x64 only.

## Review structure

The PR is split into seven commits:

1. shared resource runtime;
2. analyzer-only resource generator;
3. managed resource-owner migration;
4. Embedded NativeAOT provider integration;
5. external NativeAOT resource modes;
6. validation/performance tooling; and
7. documentation and contributor guidance.

Issues.Title: Fix dotnet test validation with explicit paths
Issues.Body:
`dotnet test` provides helpful validation when a project, solution, directory, or test module is passed as a non-first unmatched argument. That validation is misleading when an explicit build path such as `--project` is already present, because subsequent unmatched tokens belong to the test application and may legitimately name an existing project file.

This change keeps positional inference and duplicate-path validation intact, but skips the non-first path diagnostic when `--project`, `--solution`, or `--test-modules` has already selected the build input. As a result, extension option values behave consistently with and without the `--` separator.

The end-to-end test from #56369 now runs a real Microsoft.Testing.Platform project in both forms. Existing validation tests continue to verify the helpful diagnostics when no explicit build path is supplied.

Related to #56338. The .NET 10 servicing fix is in #56374.

Issues.Title: [release/10.0.4xx] Fix dotnet test argument isolation after --
Issues.Body:
SDK 10 incorrectly treats an existing project path forwarded after `--` as a positional project. For example, `dotnet test --project TestProject.csproj -- --publish-azdo-run-name TestProject.csproj` can fail with the guidance to specify the project via `--project`, even though the second path belongs to the test application.

This narrowly ports the separator-aware parsing behavior from release/11.0.1xx/main. MTP `GetBuildOptions` now isolates unmatched tokens before `--`, runs binlog argument separation only on that prefix, reconstructs the forwarded arguments with the literal suffix, and limits positional path scanning to the pre-separator argument count.

The release-specific adaptation preserves the SDK 10 implementation shape: it uses `List<string>` and `LoggerUtility.SeparateBinLogArguments`. The shared `TrySplitApplicationArgumentsAtDoubleDash` helper was added without pulling unrelated file-based app or Native AOT work.

Validation:
- The new end-to-end regression failed before the product fix with `Specifying a project for 'dotnet test' should be via '--project'.`
- The regression passes after the fix and reports zero selected tests as expected.
- The focused CLI build succeeds with 0 warnings and 0 errors.
- 10 adjacent first-unmatched-token positional path cases pass.

Fixes: #56338

This is a manual backport because automatic `/backport` workflow run [35606166997](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/actions/runs/35606166997) failed without creating a pull request.

## Description

Unifies `dotnet watch` browser tools behind the application-origin provider contract from #56118. Issues.Title: Run ResolvePackageFileConflicts tests in parallel without mutating CWD
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Allows `GivenAResolvePackageFileConflictsMultiThreading` to participate in the existing class-level test parallelism by eliminating its process-wide current-directory mutation instead of replacing `[DoNotParallelize]` with narrower resource locks.

## Why

`[ResourceLock(WellKnownResources.CurrentDirectory)]` only coordinates tests that declare the same lock. It does not protect unannotated tests in the assembly that read relative paths or capture the current directory, so changing this class from `[DoNotParallelize]` to resource locks could still interfere with concurrently running classes.

The tests do not need to change the process CWD to verify `TaskEnvironment.ProjectDirectory` path resolution. Their files already live under unique project directories. This change:

- removes all `Directory.GetCurrentDirectory` and `Directory.SetCurrentDirectory` calls from the class;
- removes the three `CurrentDirectory` resource locks;
- uses unique relative manifest and targeting-pack paths so accidental process-CWD resolution cannot find a coincidentally existing path; and
- retains cleanup of each test instance's unique root.

This removes the shared resource entirely, which is the preferred parallelization approach in `test/AGENTS.md`.

## Validation

```text
.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe scripts\RunTests.cs -- --project test\Microsoft.NET.Build.Tasks.Tests\Microsoft.NET.Build.Tasks.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~GivenAResolvePackageFileConflictsMultiThreading" --skip-redist-check --repeat 10
```

Result: 10/10 runs passed, 3 tests per run. The project built with 0 warnings and 0 errors.

A temporary unannotated test continuously verified that the process CWD remained stable while this class ran under `MSTestParallelizeScope=ClassLevel`; the combined run passed 10/10. The temporary probe was removed after validation.

Issues.Title: [release/11.0.1xx] Bundle Roslyn ProjectData tasks and import them through the SDK (#56243)
Issues.Body:
Backport of [the PR from main](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/pull/56243) which needed hand merge resolution in the version.props files.

## Description

This adds a new feature to the SDK for producing lscache files during a build. These files are currently built by DevKit with MSBuild tasks and targets that are injected into builds by the DevKit extension; this simply moves those tasks/targets into the SDK. The feature is currently gated behind an MSBuild property which off by default.

The eventual customer impact is for customers who turn this feature on, doing a build and then opening an IDE will allow much faster loads, since we will have already built caches needed for fast loading.

## Regression

- [x] No -- it's a new feature behind an opt-in setting

## Risk

Low -- this code is already shipping in DevKit's release channel as of last week, and the feature is gated behind an opt-in flag.

## Testing

New automated tests were added that verify the lscache files are only created when the feature is enabled (and are not created when disabled). The CI build from this PR was also downloaded and smoke tested as well.

Issues.Title: dotnet format - AllReferencedProjectsLoadedAsync does not track already evaluated projects
Issues.Body:
### Describe the bug

I'm currently working on a legacy project that has over 120 csproj projects that have convoluted dependency chains between them. dotnet format would take fifteen minutes on this project, despite other operations not being so bad.

After some debugging, it looks like the AllReferencedProjectsLoadedAsync in AnalyzerRunner.cs was taking up most of the time. It recursively checks every project to see that it compiles, but doesn't track if a project has already been checked.

So if we had projects, A, B, C, D, E, with the following dependencies.
```
A -> B, C
B -> D, E
C -> D, E
```
Then the AllReferencedProjectsLoadedAsync code will check every possible iteration of the dependency chain,
```
A -> B -> D
       -> E
     C -> D
       -> E
```
and will check that D, E compile twice, and check all of their dependencies twice.

In our codebase, where there are lots of projects with unoptimized project-references, projects were being checked many times over, which led to minutes of unnecessary work.

A possible fix is to have a `HashSet<ProjectId>` that tracks if a project has been evaluated as 'true' to avoid unnecessary double-checking. 

```csharp
            static async Task<bool> OptimizedAllReferencedProjectsLoadedAsync(Project project, CancellationToken cancellationToken , HashSet<ProjectId> projects)
            {
                if (projects.Contains(project.Id))
                {
                    return true;
                }
                
                var compilation = await project.GetCompilationAsync(cancellationToken);
                if (compilation is null)
                    return false;

                // If we don't have a System.Object this project is clearly missing references and we shouldn't try to process it further
                if (compilation.ObjectType.TypeKind == TypeKind.Error)
                    return false;

                foreach (var projectReference in project.ProjectReferences)
                {
                    var referencedProject = project.Solution.GetProject(projectReference.ProjectId);
                    Debug.Assert(referencedProject is not null);

                    if (!await OptimizedAllReferencedProjectsLoadedAsync(referencedProject, cancellationToken, projects))
                        return false;
                }

                projects.Add(project.Id);

                return true;
            }

```

### Steps to reproduce

Simple artificial example.

Powershell script to create 30 library projects where each has a dependency on all previous ones.
```pwsh
$existingProjects=@()
foreach($i in 0..30){
    $projectName = "proj_$i"
    dotnet new classlib --name $projectName --force
    $projectPath = "$($projectName)/$($projectName).csproj"
    if($existingProjects){
        dotnet reference add --project $projectPath $existingProjects
    }
    $existingProjects += "$($projectName)/$($projectName).csproj";
}
```

### Expected behavior

Running `dotnet format style \proj_30\proj_30.csproj -v diag` takes a reasonable amount of time. There are 30 projects, but each one only contains one default file ('Class1.cs') each, so formatting shouldn't take too long.

### Actual behavior

Running `dotnet build .\proj_30\proj_30.csproj `, takes 34 seconds.
Running `dotnet format whitespace .\proj_30\proj_30.csproj `, takes 16 seconds.

Running `dotnet format style .\proj_30\proj_30.csproj` takes 11.5 minutes.

Running dotnet format style on projects in order, it starts to slow down after project 23.
```csproj
foreach($i in 0..30){
    Write-Host "Formatting proj_$i.csproj"
    Measure-Command {
        dotnet format style "./proj_$i/proj_$i.csproj" --no-restore
    }
}
```

### Is this a regression?

Not sure

### Are there any workarounds?

The code works, it's just very slow.

Issues.Title: `StaticWebAssetFingerprintPattern` defined in WasmBrowser templates is visible in the project tree
Issues.Body: ### Describe the bug `StaticWebAssetFingerprintPattern` is a MSBuild item which Include value is not a file path. Should the SDK provide an ItemDefinitionGroup for this item type, with `Visible=false` metadata, so that IDEs can distinguish it from file items? ### Steps to reproduce 1. `dotnet new install Microsoft.NET.Runtime.WebAssembly.Templates.net10` 2. `dotnet new wasmbrowser` 3. Open project in Rider 4. Observe "JS" file visible in the project root ### Expected behavior Since `StaticWebAssetFingerprintPattern` is not a file item group, it's expected to be invisible by default. Or, at least, defined in default templates with Visible="false". ### Actual behavior Even though `StaticWebAssetFingerprintPattern` is not a file item group, it's still has default Visible=true. ### Is this a regression? No ### Are there any workarounds? There are two workarounds `Visible="false"` on each include: ```xml ``` Global `ItemDefinitionGroup`: ```xml false ``` ### dotnet --info output ```console .NET SDK: Version: 11.0.100-rc.1.26425.128 Commit: 3551975be0 Workload version: 11.0.100-rc.1.26460.1 MSBuild version: 18.11.0-1.26425.128+3551975be Runtime Environment: OS Name: Mac OS X OS Version: 27.0 OS Platform: Darwin RID: osx-arm64 Base Path: /usr/local/share/dotnet/sdk/11.0.100-rc.1.26425.128 .NET workloads installed: [wasm-tools] Installation Source: SDK 11.0.100-rc.1 Manifest Version: 11.0.100-rc.1.26425.128/11.0.100-rc.1 Manifest Path: /usr/local/share/dotnet/sdk-manifests/11.0.100-rc.1/microsoft.net.workload.mono.toolchain.current/11.0.100-rc.1.26425.128/WorkloadManifest.json Install Type: FileBased ``` ### IDE version JetBrains Rider 2026.2.1 ### Other details One can say it's not an SDK issue, but Rider issue. Because Rider decides to include all ItemGroups visible in the project tree, unless these are well known not-file includes. But MSBuild also has a `` feature allowing to globally predefine default metadata, without relying on specific tooling internal filtering.

Issues.Title: Hide StaticWebAssetFingerprintPattern items by default
Issues.Body:
`StaticWebAssetFingerprintPattern` items use logical names such as `JS`, not file paths, but IDEs can still surface them as project tree entries. WebAssembly templates currently need explicit `Visible="false"` metadata to avoid showing these non-file items.

- **SDK defaults**
  - Added default `Visible=false` metadata for `StaticWebAssetFingerprintPattern` in the Static Web Assets fingerprinting patterns props.
  - Applies to SDK-provided and project/template-defined fingerprint patterns unless explicitly overridden.

  </StaticWebAssetFingerprintPattern>
</ItemDefinitionGroup>
```

- **Coverage**
  - Added a WebAssembly design-time evaluation test verifying a project-defined fingerprint pattern inherits `Visible=false`.

Issues.Title: Prevent CA1508 crashes when analyzing attribute arguments
Issues.Body:
CA1508 can throw `NullReferenceException` when a comparison appears in an attribute on an assembly or top-level type because attribute operation blocks lack the containing type expected by dataflow analysis.

- **Analyzer**
  - Check `SupportsFlowAnalysis()` before constructing dataflow contexts.
  - Skip attribute CFGs, which the shared flow framework does not support.

- **Regression coverage**
  - Cover comparison expressions in assembly attributes.
  - Cover attributes on static and non-static top-level types.
  - Verify no CA1508 or AD0001 diagnostics are produced.
